speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are suffering from chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to better assist you, could you tell me how long these symptoms have been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the relief with defecation and urgency are significant clues. Have you experienced any blood in your stool, unintentional weight loss, or a significant change in your stool caliber? Also, have you noticed any fever or night sweats recently?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome with Diarrhea (IBS-D) secondary to recent gastroenteritis.
